title: Choose the visual world
question: Replacement look for Daily Intentionality. Same job: stack blocks, 15-minute buffer, +15, export to Calendar. The cream/glass/Caslon UI is anti-reference. No image generation this round — code-led.

options.label: Period timetable
options.thesis: The day is one column of periods. Clock times are printed in the margin; you add a class, the rest of the column drops.
options.viewport: iPad landscape: left margin is the period clock, the column is the day, add-a-period controls sit as a stamp row under the heading — not a second glass app.
options.risk: Can read as homework if the grid is cute instead of bureaucratic.

raised.raise: Buffer is etched ticks between periods, a measured 15, not empty padding.
Period rows are a rigid cell mask; a block never reflows mid-glyph.
One vertical axis is the whole route home: morning at the top, export at the bottom of the column.
Crisp integer edges, no blur glass.

options.label: Departure board
options.thesis: Each intention is a departure: time, destination, duration. +15 is a delay that flips every later row.
options.viewport: A stacked board of rows. Adding a block inserts a flap. Export is ‘post the board’.
options.risk: This is the familiar ‘time as a list of departures’ landing most planner redesigns want; it can look like a novelty clock.

options.label: Deck fascia
options.thesis: One bolted fascia: every function is a labeled switch. The day is the tape that is rolling.
options.viewport: No pages. Toggles for kind, a counter for start time, presets as transport keys, timeline as the VU of the day.
options.case: Holds product clarity (one panel, labeled controls). Loses audience identification: hi-fi nerd, not morning iPad.
options.risk: Reads as a synth plugin if the metal is fake.

options.label: Quoted stockroom
options.thesis: Every zone is named in straight quotes. You are filling “THE DAY”, not a vault.
options.viewport: Quoted labels, one diagonal under the live block, orange tag on the selected preset.
options.case: Holds clarity (literal names). Loses identification: stockroom fashion, not a personal planner.
options.risk: Hazard stripes become costume if they do not mean delay or overflow.

options.label: Signal bench
options.case: A morning iPad planner is not a probe clip. Clarity as waveform fails the stack-and-export job.

options.label: Glyph scene
options.case: Sculpture-as-text does not identify as planning a day.
options.kept: Rigid cell mask: periods never reflow.

options.label: Wall dive
options.case: Scuba topology is not this user's scene; vertical poetry hides the clock.
options.kept: One vertical axis as the only route through the day.

options.label: Pixel city
options.case: A toy metropolis is not a calendar handoff.
options.kept: Crisp integer edges instead of glass blur.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A calm split-view planner: list of blocks, times, one export. The look every AI ships if you ask for a planner.
canonCard.viewport: Two cards, cream wash, Caslon title — the incumbent.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the current UI and from a thousand generated dashboards.
